name: Illusionists

identity.symbol: None officially. Personal sigils, visible only under special conditions — starlight, smoke, the corner of the eye.
identity.public_perception: Sometimes mistaken for mad prophets or charlatans. Their power seems to arise from unknown sources; they are met with cautious tolerance by the Ilmenor and unease by everyone else.

goals.primary: No collective goal. Each Illusionist pursues their own understanding of what illusions actually are and where they come from.
secondary: Pass the true cosmological understanding of illusion to the rare student who won't flinch at what the other worlds look like.
Find and reach the twenty portal vertices — the points where the twelve worlds touch.
goals.hidden_agenda: Some believe the folds between worlds can be navigated, not merely glimpsed. The portal-hunting thread is real and dangerous.

philosophy.summary: Illusions are not fabrications. They are resonance — light and form bleeding through from adjacent worlds, or generated by the magical overlap of those worlds. The twelve-world cosmology, linked by twenty portals at the vertices of a truncated dodecahedron, is the physics underlying illusionist magic. This is not trickery. Illusionists who understand this know where their magic is coming from; those who don't are working blind. The Ilmenor have not codified this because they cannot control it.
methods: Solitary practice or scattered mystery schools — no formal order.
Mentorship: the tradition passes one practitioner to the next.
Avoid tampering with forbidden truths — the line that keeps Ilmenor tolerance intact.
limits: No collective lines or limits — each practitioner sets their own.
As a practical matter: do not openly defy Ilmenor workings or disrupt their operations.

position.territory: None. Solitary shelters, hidden workshops, mystery schools in forgotten places. Tazuln's shelter north of Orziben — eleven holes in a hillside ceiling, no path — is typical.
position.active_since: Predates the Fall. The tradition survived because it was never centralized enough to be destroyed.

rivals.nature: Tolerated as a separate tradition, not classed as rogue — but regarded as dangerous artists of unreality. Disputes arise when illusions disrupt Ilmenor workings or defy natural law. The tolerance is conditional and could end.

needs: Students willing to accept the cosmological truth of what illusion actually is.
Access to places where the worlds overlap — thin spots, portal-adjacent locations.
provides: Cosmological knowledge of the twelve-world structure and portal geometry.
Seers, keepers of hidden places, agents of veiled truths.

mystery-schools.name: Scattered Mystery Schools
mystery-schools.role: Loose clusters of practitioners in forgotten places. No hierarchy, no shared doctrine beyond the cosmological understanding of resonance. Some students never find one; some find Tazuln.
mystery-schools.notes: The mystery school tradition is how the craft survives between generations. Most practitioners are solitary long before and after any formal teaching.

tazulns-shelter.name: Tazuln's Shelter
tazulns-shelter.role: The working base of the most significant known Illusionist practitioner. Hard to find — no path, eleven deliberate holes in a hillside ceiling. Tazuln teaches here, watches the worlds, and works toward finding a portal vertex before he dies.
tazulns-shelter.location: North of Orziben, built into a hillside
tazulns-shelter.notes: Tazuln opened Chekkad's training by telling him exactly which world his illusion was real in. Laid out the full twelve-world cosmology: 20 portals at the vertices of a truncated dodecahedron. Chekkad cast something and for the first time knew where it was coming from. Tazuln's portal-hunting dream is a long-term campaign thread.

dm_notes: Chekkad (Hoi) is an Illusionist — his training with Tazuln in session 26 established the twelve-world cosmology as canon. Every illusion Chekkad casts now has a physical explanation: it is real in some adjacent world. Tazuln wants to reach one of the twenty portal vertices before he dies — Chekkad's training opens that quest. The portal geometry (truncated dodecahedron, 12 worlds, 20 vertices) is available to any player who engages seriously with illusionist magic. The Ilmenor tolerate Illusionists; that tolerance has a line. The Serdanos distrust anyone tapping Faery's edge for power — Illusionists who work near the veil will draw their attention.
